subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which policy shape is approved for core?
rationale: The request changes browser egress controls and public config/UX semantics, and current source shows no existing confirm or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve a staged core policy
options.body: Start with a narrow default-strict allow/block policy and non-overridable metadata behavior before considering interactive confirmation UX.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to user-approval UX with timeout, rate-limit, redirect, DNS-rebinding, and audit semantics across browser navigation paths before implementation.

options.title: Keep current model
options.body: Leave strict default plus hostname exceptions and broad dangerous opt-in as the supported model, with clearer docs if maintainers reject more core policy surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a staged core policy
recommendation.body: Start with a narrow default-strict allow/block policy and non-overridable metadata behavior before considering interactive confirmation UX.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal across recent browser CDP/SSRF work and the broader guarded-fetch security policy surface.
